beats.care: Emergency care continues, they say. If anyone at home has a planned visit at Osmania hospital, check before you go.
beats.what: Junior doctors at Osmania General Hospital start a strike today, pausing planned outpatient visits and planned operations.
beats.why: Their association says problems with training, hospital infrastructure and working conditions stayed unfixed despite repeated requests.

cards.body: Day one: doctors protested at the hospital from 9 am to 2 pm. They want broken X-ray, endoscopy and ventilator machines fixed on a deadline, and say they may step up the protest if there's no response.
cards.title: 🆕 Evening update

cards.body: The Osmania Medical College Junior Doctors Association issued the notice on 10 October. The protest begins at 8:30 am at the hospital's main gate. Interns, students and residents from all departments were asked to join.
Interns and young doctors doing postgraduate training. In big government hospitals they handle a large share of daily patient care, so their strike is felt fast.
cards.title: who are junior doctors?

opts: Yes, it's the only way to be heard
cards.q: Is a doctors' strike fair if emergency care keeps running?
What does the association say stays open during the strike?
cards.why: The strike targets planned visits and surgeries, while emergency care is kept running.

hook: Osmania hospital's junior doctors strike today. *What still works?*
